Message:
Harden security, data protection, batch fidelity and observability

Database and schema
- Consolidate schema creation, reference data and test data into a single
  owner-applied Flyway migration set that every service validates against,
  and add the batch metadata tables.
- Encrypt the seeded personally identifiable data in place through a Java
  migration, so no plaintext SSN, government-issued id or EFT account id is
  left at rest.
- Correct composite primary-key column order, cross-reference indexes, check
  constraints and the transaction-id sequence guard so the relational model
  matches the record layouts it was derived from.

Security and session handling
- Apply one hardened filter chain across the services: anonymous requests are
  refused with 401 and authenticated requests lacking the required authority
  with 403, and management metrics require a dedicated monitoring principal
  while health and info stay open for probes.
- Hash stored credentials with a single BCrypt cost, throttle repeated failed
  sign-on attempts, revoke sessions on demand and record an audit trail of
  authentication outcomes.
- Carry the sign-on context in an externalised Redis session under one
  allowlisted JSON attribute, rotate the session id at sign-on and never
  create a session for an anonymous caller.
- Protect state-changing requests at the edge with a cookie-backed
  double-submit CSRF token.

Account, card and transaction handling
- Mask the SSN, government-issued id and EFT account id in every response and
  keep the stored value whenever a masked value is submitted back, so a
  masked field can never overwrite the data it hides.
- Compare the submitted snapshot against the stored record and the entity
  version before rewriting, reporting a concurrent modification instead of
  overwriting it, and treat a masked identifier as unchanged only when it is
  the mask of the value currently stored.
- Raise a single fail-closed error when encrypted data cannot be read or
  written, rather than returning or persisting an unusable value.

Batch processing
- Share one batch infrastructure configuration, job repository and output
  path resolver, and refuse a submission whose output paths fall outside the
  configured roots.
- Stream the daily transaction feed with a cursor reader, write rejected
  records at their exact fixed width with the legacy reason codes, and report
  the legacy return code and rejected-record tally.
- Preserve fixed-scale monetary arithmetic in interest calculation, including
  the fallback disclosure group, and generate statements at their exact line
  widths.
- Fail a posting run that completes without reading any records, so an empty
  feed cannot be mistaken for a successful day.

Observability
- Emit structured JSON logs carrying the service name, correlation id, trace
  id and span id, with appenders declared inside the profile that references
  them.
- Expose health, liveness, readiness, info and Prometheus endpoints with
  bounded datastore timeouts so an outage surfaces as a readiness failure
  while liveness stays up, and echo the correlation id exactly once.
- Add the Prometheus scrape configuration and a Grafana dashboard covering
  request, datastore and batch metrics.

Build, packaging and deployment
- Split unit and integration test execution, add schema-backed integration
  fixtures and broaden coverage across the services.
- Pin container images, grant each service its own database role, document
  the local environment variables required to start the stack, and update the
  Kubernetes manifests and build context exclusions to match.

Documentation
- Record the decisions taken and keep the source-to-target traceability
  matrix aligned with the delivered implementation.
